newsitem.title: USA: Levitt meets muni groups April 24 on yield burning.
newsitem.headline: Levitt meets muni groups April 24 on yield burning.

text.p: Seven key state and local government groups are set to meet April 24 with SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt to urge him to support a revamping of the Clinton Administration's strategy on yield burning, a knowledgeable industry source said.

The groups, including National Governors Association and U.S. Conference of Mayors, want the administration to "back off" of a yield burning settlement option it offered states and localities last year and to convene the President's Working Group on Financial Markets to make policy on the issue.

The "Big Seven" state and local government groups wrote Levitt on March 18 to request a meeting because he is part of the President's influential working group, set up to examine the 1987 stock market crash and then reestablished in 1994 to addressed broader market issues.
The working group is chaired by the Treasury Department secretary and includes the heads of SEC, Federal Reserve Board and Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
Yield burning refers to allegations that bond underwriters overcharge states and localities for U.S. Treasury securities they bought to help them refinance outstanding bonds.
The Internal Revenue Service told municipalities last year that they can avoid having bonds declared taxable by settling any overcharges with the agency now.

But muni groups told Donald Lubick, Treasury's assistant secretary, at a Jan 27 meeting that the vast majority of localities were unaware of any yield burning. They said that the SEC's enforcement staff, not IRS, should assume the lead on the issue by taking legal action against guilty bond underwriters.
Big Seven aides say the group has received no response from Lubick, or from Marcia Hale, a special assistant to Clinton who the groups contacted on March 20 for assistance on the issue.

Big Seven groups argue that the SEC already is pursuing major yield burning investigations in at least 20 cases involving bond underwriters and that SEC action would recover losses to the U.S. Treasury and to affected states and localities.
An SEC spokesman was not available.

Other Big Seven members are the National Association of Counties, National Conference of State Legislatures, National League of Cities, Council of State Governments and International City/County Management Association.
